report.source_text: Due to disseminated tumor disease in multiple non-resectable locations, a palliative systemical chemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2)/carboplatin (AUC 6) was started by the oncological outpatient clinic (Fig. 4). Priorly, Trenantone® 130 mg subcutaneously for ovary protection was administered. Furthermore, an osteoprotective bisphosphonate therapy with Zometa® 4 mg was begun. Regarding the bone metastases in the right scapula and in the 3rd thoracic vertebral body, no surgical intervention but radiotherapy was planned in the further course as part of the palliative therapy regimen.

clinician.final_diagnosis: A NUT midline carcinoma was diagnosed by immunohistochemistry (Table 1) while FISH analysis did not show the typical NUT gene rearrangements due to cryptic translocation.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old pregnant woman presented with right shoulder pain, persistent dyspnea, cough, and hemoptysis. A chest X-ray revealed a tumor mass in the right lung (E001). Subsequent MRI scans showed multiple suspicious lesions in the right lung, mediastinum, right scapula, and an osteolytic lesion of the 3rd thoracic vertebral body (E003). Biopsies were performed, including a fine-needle biopsy of the pulmonary mass and an open biopsy of the scapula lesion after a cesarean section (E004). Pathology confirmed a NUT midline carcinoma by immunohistochemistry, with FISH analysis indicating cryptic translocation despite not showing typical NUT gene rearrangements (E004). A post-cesarean section PET-CT revealed additional metastases in both breasts (E005). Due to disseminated disease, palliative systemic chemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin was initiated, along with ovary protection and bisphosphonate therapy, and radiotherapy was planned for bone metastases (E006). After five courses of chemotherapy, the patient showed a decline in dyspnea, and a PET-CT 3 months later demonstrated partial remission of known metastases in the right lung and both breasts (E007).

MRI scans revealed multiple suspicious lesions in the right lung, mediastinum, right scapula, and an osteolytic lesion of the 3rd thoracic vertebral body.
A fine-needle biopsy of the pulmonary tumor mass and an open biopsy of the right side scapula tumor lesion were performed.
A NUT midline carcinoma was diagnosed by immunohistochemistry, and FISH analysis indicated cryptic translocation despite not showing typical NUT gene rearrangements.
PET-CT performed after cesarean section showed further multiple metastases in both mammae in addition to the known tumor lesions.

Palliative systemic chemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin was started due to disseminated tumor disease, along with ovary protection and bisphosphonate therapy, and radiotherapy was planned for bone metastases.
After five courses of chemotherapy, the patient showed a decline of dyspnea, and a PET-CT 3 months after therapy demonstrated a partial remission of known metastases.
